message.content:
For  

\[
ax^{\,2}+bx+c=0 \quad\text{with}\quad a=1,\;b=2,\;c=3
\]

the quadratic formula gives  

\[
x=\frac{-b\pm\sqrt{\,b^{2}-4ac\,}}{2a}
   =\frac{-2\;\pm\;\sqrt{\,4-12\,}}{2}
   =\frac{-2\;\pm\;\sqrt{-8}}{2}.
\]

Since \(D=b^{2}-4ac=-8<0\), there are **no real roots**—only complex ones:

\[
\sqrt{-8}=i\sqrt{8}=i\,2\sqrt{2},
\]
so

\[
x=\frac{-2}{2}\;\pm\;\frac{i\,2\sqrt{2}}{2}
  =-1\;\pm\;i\sqrt{2}.
\]

Hence the two (complex conjugate) solutions are  

\[
\boxed{x_1=-1+i\sqrt{2}}, \qquad 
\boxed{x_2=-1-i\sqrt{2}}\,. 
\]

Compute: sqrt(-8)=i*sqrt(8) = i * 2√2? Actually √8 = 2√2 ≈ 2.828427124746190097603377448419396157... So root: (-2 ± i*2√2)/2 = -1 ± i√2.

Thus solutions: x = -1 + i√2 or x = -1 - i√2.
